newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa exports to U.S. seen in slump.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa exports to U.S. seen in slump.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa bean exports to the United States plunged last year due to stringent quality checks forcing local exporters to other markets, and are likely to be down this year, an industry official said Wednesday.
Exports to the United States fell to 46,663 metric tons in 1995 from 79,434 tons the previous year, Siswoputranto, executive director of the Indonesia Cocoa Association, said.
"Direct exports to the United States are likely to be weaker this year as well," he said. He did not have export projections for this year.
Siswoputranto said Indonesian exporters had increased sales to markets in Eastern Europe, the Middle East and China where quality checks were less stringent.
The United States is the single largest market for cocoa from Indonesia, the world's third largest cocoa producer after the Ivory Coast and Ghana.
Siswoputranto said efforts had been made to improve the quality of overseas-bound cocoa by ensuring only professional and accredited companies carried out fumigation for insects in Indonesia.
